title: Regular and irregular plurals
somali: Magacyada badankood waxay qaataan -s (cats). Qaar waa lawadaa: man→men, child→children.
explanation: Add -s to most nouns. Add -es after s, sh, ch, x (box → boxes). Some plurals are irregular: man → men, child → children, foot → feet.
examples: Two cats are on the sofa.
The children are happy.
I have two boxes.

exercises.prompt: One child, two ___.
One box, two ___.
Correct the sentence: I have three childs.
Order the words.

title: Past simple: regular and irregular verbs
somali: Waqtigii hore: erayada joogtada ah waxay qaataan -ed (worked). Qaar waa lawadaa: go→went.
explanation: Use the past simple for finished actions. Regular verbs add -ed (work → worked). Irregular verbs change: go → went, see → saw. Questions and negatives use did + base verb.
examples: I worked yesterday.
She went to school.
Did you see him?
mistakes: Say 'I didn't go', not 'I didn't went'.

exercises.prompt: Yesterday I ___ a film.
She ___ (go) home early.
Correct the sentence: He didn't went to work.
exercises.explain: After didn't use the base verb.
accept: He did not go to work.

exercises.prompt: Order the words.
exercises.explain: Question word + did + subject + base verb.

title: Comparatives and superlatives
somali: Is barbar: taller than. Ugu sarreeya: the tallest.
explanation: Short adjectives add -er / -est (tall → taller → tallest). Long adjectives use more / most (expensive → more expensive → most expensive). Use 'than' after a comparative.
examples: My brother is taller than me.
This is the most interesting book.
Today is hotter than yesterday.

exercises.prompt: This bag is ___ than that one.
She is the ___ (good) student in class.
Correct the sentence: He is more taller than me.
Order the words.

title: First conditional
somali: Haddii (if) + hadda → mustaqbalka: If it rains, I will stay home.
explanation: Use if + present simple for a real possibility, and will + base verb for the result: If it rains, I will stay at home.
examples: If you study, you will pass.
If she calls, I will tell her.
We will be late if we don't hurry.
mistakes: Don't use 'will' after if: say 'If it rains', not 'If it will rain'.

exercises.prompt: If I ___ time, I will call you.
If it rains, we ___ (stay) inside.
Correct the sentence: If you will come, I will help.
exercises.answer: If you come, I will help.

exercises.prompt: Order the words.

title: Present passive
somali: Falka la sameeyo: English is spoken here. (is/are + past participle)
explanation: Form the passive with be + past participle. Use it when the action matters more than who does it: English is spoken here.
examples: Rice is grown in many countries.
The shop is closed on Sundays.
These cars are made in Japan.
mistakes: Use the past participle: 'is made', not 'is make'.

exercises.prompt: Coffee ___ in Ethiopia.
These books ___ (write) by a famous author.
Correct the sentence: The letter is write every day.
exercises.answer: The letter is written every day.

exercises.prompt: Order the words.

title: Second and third conditional
somali: Second: If I had money, I would travel (ma jirto). Third: If I had studied, I would have passed (waa dhacay).
explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base verb (unreal present or future). Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle (unreal past).
examples: If I were rich, I would travel.
If she had left earlier, she would have caught the train.
mistakes: Use 'were' for all persons in formal second conditionals.

exercises.prompt: If I ___ you, I would apologise.
If he had studied, he ___ passed.
Correct the sentence: If I would have known, I would have helped.
exercises.answer: If I had known, I would have helped.

exercises.prompt: Order the words.

title: Reported speech
somali: Hadalka la soo guuriyo: 'I am tired' → She said she was tired (waqtiga dib baa loo celiyaa).
explanation: When reporting, verbs usually shift back one tense: am → was, will → would, present perfect → past perfect. Pronouns and time words change too.
examples: 'I am busy,' he said → He said he was busy.
'I will call,' she said → She said she would call.
mistakes: Don't keep the original tense: 'He said he was tired', not 'He said he is tired' (in most cases).

exercises.prompt: 'I will help you,' she said. → She said she ___ help me.
'I am tired,' he said. → He said he ___ tired.
Correct the sentence: She said she will come tomorrow.
exercises.answer: She said she would come the next day.
accept: She said she would come tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Order the words.

title: Inversion after negative adverbials
somali: Marka xaaladaha diidmo hore loo dhigo, fal-gaarigu wuu horreeyaa: Never have I seen...
explanation: After negative or restrictive adverbials (never, rarely, not only, hardly) at the start of a sentence, use question word order: Never have I seen such a view.
examples: Rarely do we eat out.
Not only did she win, but she also broke the record.
Hardly had he arrived when it began to rain.
mistakes: Don't keep normal order: 'Never I have seen', say 'Never have I seen'.

exercises.prompt: Rarely ___ late.
Not only ___ she sing, but she also dances. (does/did)
exercises.explain: Use do/does/did when there is no auxiliary.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Never I have seen such a mess.
exercises.answer: Never have I seen such a mess.

exercises.prompt: Order the words.

title: Wish and if only
somali: Wish waxaa loo isticmaalaa quusasho: I wish I had more time. I wish I had studied.
explanation: Use wish + past simple for present regrets (I wish I had a car). Use wish + past perfect for past regrets (I wish I had studied). Use wish + would for annoying habits.
examples: I wish I knew the answer.
She wishes she had called him.
I wish you would stop talking.
mistakes: Don't use present tense after wish: 'I wish I knew', not 'I wish I know'.

exercises.prompt: I wish I ___ more free time now.
She wishes she ___ studied harder. (past perfect)
exercises.explain: wish + past perfect for past regret.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I wish I have a bigger house.
exercises.answer: I wish I had a bigger house.

exercises.prompt: Order the words.

title: The mandative subjunctive
somali: Ka dib falalka sida suggest/insist, isticmaal foomka aasaasiga ah: I suggest that he be early.
explanation: After verbs like suggest, insist, demand, recommend (and adjectives like essential), the clause may use the base form of the verb: It is essential that she be present.
examples: I insist that he apologise.
The board recommended that the policy be revised.
It is vital that every student attend.
mistakes: The base form has no -s: 'that he attend', not 'that he attends' (formal).

exercises.prompt: They demanded that he ___ immediately.
It is essential that she ___ on time. (be)
Correct the sentence: I suggest that he goes now.
exercises.answer: I suggest that he go now.

exercises.prompt: Order the words.

title: Cleft sentences for emphasis
somali: Weedh ku xooga leh: It was John who broke the window.
explanation: Cleft sentences put emphasis on one part. It-cleft: It was Maria who called. Wh-cleft: What I need is a rest.
examples: It was the noise that woke me up.
What annoys me is the delay.
It is honesty that matters most.
mistakes: Keep the relative word: 'It was John who...', not 'It was John he...'.

exercises.prompt: It was Sara ___ won the prize.
___ I need is a holiday.
Correct the sentence: It was the delay what annoyed me.
exercises.answer: It was the delay that annoyed me.

exercises.prompt: Order the words.
